name: Question 6
problem:
Let $f(x)$ be the $8$-periodic extension of the function $F(x)=\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}+4$ defined on $[-4,4).$  Select the correct options in the reasoning below, showing the derivation of the Fourier series of the $8$-periodic extension of $G(x)=x$ from the corresponding Fourier series of $f(x).$The Fourier series of $f(x)$ is given by

$$
\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}+4∼\frac{20}{3}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{32(-1)^{n}}{{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}}{{field-1}}.
$$

Since $f$ is  
{{field-2}}
and  
{{field-3}}
on $R,$ we may differentiate its Fourier series term-by-term to get

$$
x∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{{field-4}}\cdot {{field-5}}.
$$
worked_solution:
First, notice that $F(x)$ is an even function. So, the Fourier series of its $2L$-periodic extension has the form

$$
\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}cos\,(\frac{n\pi x}{L}).
$$

In our case, $L=4.$ Thus, the Fourier series of $f(x)$ is given by

$$
f(x)∼\frac{20}{3}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{32(-1)^{n}}{{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}}cos\,(\frac{n\pi x}{4}).
$$

Now, notice that  

- the function $F$ is continuously differentiable on $(-4,4),$

- continuous on $[-4,4),$ and

- satisfies $F(-4)=F(4),$ if we extend the value at $x=4$ using the formula $F(x)=\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}+4.$

Therefore, the $8$-periodic extension $f$ is
$\text{continuous}$ and
$\text{piecewise smooth}$
on $R,$ so we may differentiate its Fourier series term-by-term:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{d}{dx}\,(\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}+4) & ∼\frac{d}{dx}\,(\frac{20}{3})+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{d}{dx}(\frac{32(-1)^{n}}{{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}}cos\,(\frac{n\pi x}{4})) \\ x & ∼0+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{32(-1)^{n}}{{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}}(-\frac{n\pi }{4}sin\,(\frac{n\pi x}{4})) \\ x & ∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{-8(-1)^{n}}{n\pi }sin\,(\frac{n\pi x}{4}) \\ x & ∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{8(-1)^{n+1}}{n\pi }\cdot sin\,(\frac{n\pi x}{4}).\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

First, notice that F(x) is an even function. So, the Fourier series of its 2L-periodic extension has the form a02+∑n=1∞ancos(nπxL).

In our case, L=4. Thus, the Fourier series of f(x) is given by f(x)∼203+∑n=1∞32(−1)nn2π2cos(nπx4).

Now, notice that

  • the function F is continuously differentiable on (−4,4),

  • continuous on [−4,4), and

  • satisfies F(−4)=F(4), if we extend the value at x=4 using the formula F(x)=12x2+4.

Therefore, the 8-periodic extension f is continuous and piecewise smooth on R, so we may differentiate its Fourier series term-by-term:

ddx(12x2+4)∼ddx(203)+∑n=1∞ddx(32(−1)nn2π2cos(nπx4))x∼0+∑n=1∞32(−1)nn2π2(−nπ4sin(nπx4))x∼∑n=1∞−8(−1)nnπsin(nπx4)x∼∑n=1∞8(−1)n+1nπ⋅sin(nπx4).
